description: Find a cover for every game whose art exists on the server. Three changes, all in the fallback search: (A) a cover list per (system, folder) instead of one box art list per system, searched in the existing preference order Named_Boxarts, Named_Titles, Named_Snaps, with a folder's list downloaded only when the cheaper ones produced no match; (B) after exact normalised equality fails, a token-sequence alignment that accepts a contiguous prefix or suffix with hard guards, which is what matches "Simpsons, The - Krusty's Fun House (U) [!].gg" to the server's "Krusty's Fun House (USA, Europe).png"; (C) a bounded cross-system fallback, last, with honest provenance. Plus (E) a miss recorded only when every avenue answered no, and (F) status lines that name the avenue. Auto-selection stays exactly as noisy as it is today: first hit wins, silently, and an ambiguous alignment auto-picks nothing.
steps: ArtworkIndex.swift, ArtworkIndexNames, the article inversion. Add `static func uninvertArticle(_ value: String) -> String` and call it inside `normalisedTitle` AFTER `ArtworkNames.stripTags` and BEFORE the diacritic fold, so it sees the comma while it is still there. The rule: find `,` followed by optional whitespace and one of `The`, `A`, `An` (case insensitive) where that article is followed by end of string or by ` - `, and rewrite `<head>, The<tail>` as `The <head><tail>`. Narrow on purpose: a comma that is not an article boundary is left alone. Both sides of every match go through `normalisedTitle`, so this makes No-Intro's "Simpsons, The - Bart vs. the World" and the other convention's "The Simpsons - Bart vs. the World" land on the same key, and it is a PREREQUISITE for the alignment below: without it the Krusty file normalises to "simpsons the krustys fun house" and the alignment residue is split across the string.

ArtworkIndex.swift, the alignment. Add to ArtworkIndexNames: `static func titleTokens(_ title: String) -> [String]` (split the normalised title on single spaces, which is safe because `collapse` has already run); `static func isSequenceMarker(_ word: String) -> Bool` (true when every character is a decimal digit, or the word is one of i, ii, iii, iv, v, vi, vii, viii, ix, x); and `static func aligns(query: [String], listing: [String]) -> Bool`. The rule, in this order: reject when either side is empty; accept nothing through equality here (equality is `match(title:in:)` and runs first); take the SHORTER side and the LONGER side; reject unless the shorter side is a contiguous PREFIX or a contiguous SUFFIX of the longer; reject when the shorter side has fewer than 2 words; reject when the shorter side joined with single spaces is fewer than 8 characters; take the residue, the longer side's remaining words in order, and reject when every residue word is a sequence marker, and reject when the residue's FIRST or LAST word is a sequence marker. Never a mid-string substring, never an edit distance, never a similarity score. Document each guard with the case it kills: the 2-word and 8-character guards stop `the` and `super` matching half a library; the sequence-marker guard is what stops "Sonic Drift 2" taking "Sonic Drift"'s cover and "Chuck Rock II - Son of Chuck" taking "Chuck Rock"'s, while still letting "Desert Strike - Return to the Gulf" match "Desert Strike" and "Taito Chase H.Q." match "Chase H.Q.", all four of which are real entries in the saved Game Gear listing.

ArtworkIndex.swift, the two search entry points. Add `static func alignedTitles(for query: String, in map: [String: String]) -> [String]` returning every map KEY that aligns with the query, sorted ascending so the result is deterministic, and `static func uniqueAlignedMatch(for query: String, in map: [String: String]) -> String?` returning the single aligned key's FILENAME when exactly one key aligns and nil when none or two or more do. The nil-on-ambiguity behaviour is the auto-selection guard: two candidates is a user choice, not a coin flip, and FEAT-003 offers both in the chooser.

ArtworkIndex.swift, the per-folder list identity. Add `static func listFilename(system: GameSystem, folder: ThumbnailFolder) -> String` to ArtworkIndexNames returning "\(system.rawValue)-\(folder.rawValue).json" (for example gg-Named_Titles.json). It lives in the pure enum so the harness can assert it. Add `let schema: Int` to ArtworkCoverList with a `static let currentSchema = 2` constant, encoded and decoded: a list written by the previous build has no schema key, so decoding fails, `stored` returns nil and the list is downloaded again under its new per-folder name. That is deliberate, because this feature changes `normalisedTitle` and a map keyed with the old normalisation would silently miss.

ArtworkIndex.swift, ArtworkCoverLists per (system, folder). Change `fileURL`, `stored`, `list` and `download` to take `folder: ThumbnailFolder` and use `ArtworkIndexNames.listFilename`. `stored` must reject a list whose `directory` does not match the current table, whose `folder` does not match the folder asked for, whose `schema` is not current, or whose age is past the unchanged 30 day `lifetime`. `download` must pass the folder to `ArtworkNames.listingURL(system:folder:)` (the parameter already exists) and must record `folder: folder.rawValue`. Every failure string must name the folder in user words, using `ThumbnailFolder.readableName`, for example "the Game Gear title screen list could not be downloaded: there is no network", so the three folders never write the same sentence. Keep the separate 180 second `session`, keep the storage location under Application Support/Artwork/CoverLists.

ArtworkIndex.swift, legacy cleanup. When a per-folder list is written successfully, delete a leftover "\(system.rawValue).json" from the previous build if it is there, so the Settings size read-out stops counting bytes nothing will ever read again. Report nothing for it: it is housekeeping, not an event. `clear()` and `usage()` already walk the whole directory and need no change.

ArtworkIndex.swift, the off-main-actor scan. Add `static func search(title: String, in list: ArtworkCoverList) async -> (exact: String?, aligned: [String], uniqueAligned: String?)` to ArtworkCoverLists. It is a non-isolated async function, exactly as the file header says `stored` and `download` are, so scanning 409 Game Gear titles or 13,418 NES ones happens off the main actor instead of inside the frame the library is drawing. The store must go through this rather than calling the pure functions directly from its @MainActor body.

GameArtwork.swift, one-folder candidates. Add a `folders: [ThumbnailFolder]` parameter (defaulting to `ThumbnailFolder.allCases`, so existing callers are untouched) to the private shared `candidates(system:forms:)` builder and expose it on `candidates(system:thumbnailName:form:folders:)`. The list search needs to ask ONE folder for a name its list says is in that folder: asking the other two would be requests the list has already answered. Keep the URL dedupe and the tier labels exactly as they are.

GameArtwork.swift, the cross-system order. Add `static let crossSystemListOrder: [GameSystem]` to SystemArtwork, ordered by the MEASURED size of each system's Named_Boxarts listing, cheapest first: sms, gg, gb, gbc, genesis, snes, gba, ps1, nes. Put the measured bytes in the comment (sms 153572, gg 240387, gb 442588, gbc 452020, genesis 618548, snes 970863, gba 1769226, ps1 2550183, nes 4054023, total 11261410) and say they were measured with curl from the build host, not estimated. Cheapest first is the whole bound: a cross-system search pays for the smallest lists before the large ones, and because lists persist for thirty days the cost converges to zero across a library.

ArtworkStore.swift, re-key the list cache. `coverLists` and `coverListTasks` become keyed on `"\(system.rawValue)#\(folder.rawValue)"` through a private `listKey(system:folder:)` helper, and `coverList(for:folder:title:phase:)` takes the folder. THE RACE RULE IS UNCHANGED AND LOAD BEARING: the `coverLists[key]` read, the `coverListTasks[key]` read and the `coverListTasks[key] = task` insert must have NO await between them, so ten cards asking at once still produce one download per (system, folder). The disk read and the download stay INSIDE the task for the same reason.

ArtworkStore.swift, phase 1: the game's own system, all three folders. Rewrite `searchCoverList` as an ordered walk. For folder in `ThumbnailFolder.allCases` (box art, title screen, in-game shot): obtain that (system, folder) list; increment `listSearchesThisRun` once per folder actually searched; ask `ArtworkCoverLists.search`; on an exact match or a unique alignment, build the candidate for THAT folder only via the new `folders:` parameter, filter out any address the ladder already walked, acquire `ArtworkGate`, fetch, release, and `keep` it. Move to the next folder ONLY when this one produced no usable match, so a game whose box art is listed costs exactly one list, which is the cost discipline the brief asks for. Record on each folder whether the list FAILED to download, in a `listFailure: String?` that survives the walk.

ArtworkStore.swift, phase 2: cross-system, last. Reached only when all three of the game's own folders answered absent. Two passes. FREE PASS: every (system, folder) list that is already in `coverLists` or already on disk, for every system except the game's own, in a deterministic order (`SystemArtwork.crossSystemListOrder` crossed with `ThumbnailFolder.allCases`, box art of each system before any title screen), searched with no download at all. PAID PASS: download at most TWO further Named_Boxarts lists, walking `crossSystemListOrder`, skipping the game's own system and anything already tried, stopping at the first hit. Justify the bound in the comment: two is the number that keeps a single unmatched game under about 700 KB in the worst case at the cheap end of the order while still making progress, and because every list persists for thirty days and is shared by every later game, a library converges on the free pass instead of paying again. The same matching and the same uniqueness guard apply; an ambiguous cross-system alignment auto-picks nothing.

ArtworkStore.swift, honest cross-system provenance. When a cross-system candidate is the one that resolves, the store (which is the only place that knows both the game's system and the list's system) overrides the provenance it hands to `keep` with "\(folder.readableName) from \(otherSystem.displayName)", for example "box art from Game Boy", and the tier with "\(folder.tier)-indexed-\(otherSystem.rawValue)". Never present another console's cover as this one's: the detail sheet's Source row reads that provenance string, so this is the sentence a user sees.

ArtworkStore.swift, the honest miss path (E). Extend the private `CoverListSearch` enum with `.ambiguousOnly(count: Int)` and return it when some folder or system aligned two or more titles and nothing was ever auto-picked. In `resolve`: `.searchedAndAbsent` still records a miss, and its status line must now say the ladder, all three folders and the cross-system search all answered no; `.ambiguousOnly` does NOT record a miss and writes its own distinct line saying how many covers matched the title and that opening the game's card can choose between them; `.searchFailed` still records nothing. If any list in the walk failed to download, the outcome must be `.searchFailed(listFailure)` rather than `.searchedAndAbsent`, because a list that failed to download is never evidence of a miss.

ArtworkStore.swift, status lines (F). Extend `announceListDownload` to take the folder and whether this is the game's own system or a cross-system attempt, so the announce-before-download behaviour covers all of the new lists: name the system, the folder in user words, and the fact that it is a few megabytes, kept, and not downloaded again for a month. Keep the once-per-run promotion to the main status line via `announcedListDownload`. Every avenue that FINDS a cover writes its own line naming that avenue: the ladder as today, "the Game Gear title screen list matched it to Krusty's Fun House (USA, Europe).png", and "the Game Boy box art list matched it, so this is box art from Game Boy". Add a `crossSystemMatchesThisRun` counter beside `listMatchesThisRun` and surface it in `coverListLine`.

SettingsScreen.swift, extend what is already there (do NOT add a second set of controls). Rewrite the second SettingsNote so it describes what actually happens now: the list is per system AND per folder, box art first, then the title screen, then the in-game shot, one folder downloaded only when the cheaper ones found nothing; a game whose own system has nothing anywhere is looked for in other systems' lists, cheapest list first, at most two extra downloads per game, and a cover found that way says which system it came from; the NES box art list is about 4 MB and its title screen and in-game shot lists are about 4.9 MB each, which are the real measured figures. Keep the existing first disclosure about filenames going to thumbnails.libretro.com. Keep ONE "Forget the downloaded cover lists" button and make its copy say it clears all of them, per system and per folder, which is what `ArtworkCoverLists.clear()` already does by emptying the directory.

project.yml: no new file is strictly required by this feature, but if you split the alignment into a new .swift file it MUST be added under targets.Continuum.sources with a comment saying what it is. Preferred: keep it in ArtworkIndex.swift beside the normaliser it depends on, and update that file's header comment to describe the three folders, the alignment and the cross-system rung.

Harness: extend .work/artwork-probe/make-harness.py to extract the declarations this feature adds or changes (ArtworkIndexNames and SystemArtwork are already extracted; add ArtworkCoverList if a check needs it, and keep the extraction working, which means every pure declaration stays a COLUMN-0 enum or struct ending in a column-0 brace). Add checks to main.swift, all of which must pass: (1) the real saved gg-Named_Titles.html parses to 834 png names and its title map contains the Krusty entry; (2) `Simpsons, The - Krusty's Fun House (U) [!].gg` unique-aligns to `Krusty's Fun House (USA, Europe).png` in all three saved Game Gear listings, and `uniqueAlignedMatch` returns exactly that filename; (3) `The Simpsons - Bart vs. the World` and `Simpsons, The - Bart vs. the World` normalise EQUAL, and both exact-match the real listing entry `Simpsons, The - Bart vs. the World (World).png` with no alignment needed; (4) a 1-word short side does not align (Batman versus Batman Returns) and a short side under 8 characters does not align (sonic 2 versus sonic 2 championship); (5) the sequence-marker guard rejects Sonic Drift 2 against Sonic Drift and Chuck Rock II - Son of Chuck against Chuck Rock, while Desert Strike - Return to the Gulf against Desert Strike and Taito Chase H.Q. against Chase H.Q. still align, all against the real saved listing; (6) a hand-built map with two distinct aligning titles returns nil from `uniqueAlignedMatch` and BOTH titles from `alignedTitles`; (7) `Super Mario World (U) [!].smc` still yields the regionTranslated rung `Super Mario World (USA)` with `Named_Boxarts` first and tier `boxart-region`, proving the cheap path still resolves with no list download; (8) `listFilename(system: .gg, folder: .title)` is `gg-Named_Titles.json`; (9) `crossSystemListOrder` holds all nine systems exactly once, cheapest measured listing first.

Verify, then commit. Run every gate in the verification list. Then commit locally on branch ios-ui-player-controls with a message in the repository's voice, for example "Search every folder the server has, and match a title that carries its series name", a body that names both bugs, the measured Krusty facts, the alignment rule with its guards, and the cross-system bound. Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: The fallback search downloads and persists a list per (system, folder): the on-disk name for Game Gear title screens is gg-Named_Titles.json, and a stored list whose folder, playlist directory, schema or age does not match is rejected and re-downloaded
A folder's list is downloaded only after the cheaper folders produced no match for that game, so a game whose box art is listed still costs exactly one list download

One download per (system, folder) is still enforced by a task dictionary with no await between the read and the insert, and list downloads still run OUTSIDE ArtworkGate while cover fetches still run inside it

Exact normalised equality is still tried first; the token alignment runs only after it fails, accepts only a contiguous prefix or suffix, and rejects a shorter side under 2 words or under 8 characters, a residue that is all sequence markers, and a residue beginning or ending with a sequence marker
An alignment that hits two or more distinct listing titles auto-picks nothing and the game falls through with no miss recorded and its own status line

The cross-system fallback runs only after all three folders of the game's own system answered absent, searches lists already on disk before downloading anything, downloads at most two further box art lists per game in ascending measured listing size, and labels what it finds "<folder> from <system>"
A miss is recorded only after the ladder, all three own-system folders and the cross-system search all answered no; a list that failed to download produces .searchFailed and no miss
Every list download is announced before it starts, naming the system and the folder; every avenue that finds a cover writes a distinct status line naming that avenue

Settings still has exactly one artwork section, one disclosure pair and one "Forget the downloaded cover lists" button, with copy that describes per-folder and cross-system lists and the real measured sizes
swiftc -frontend -parse exits 0 for every .swift file under native/ios/, project.yml parses, no .swift file is unlisted, and cargo test still reports 74 passed
The offline harness passes, including all nine new checks named in the steps
verification: cd native/ios && for f in *.swift; do swiftc -frontend -parse "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "ok $f" || echo "FAIL $f"; done

python3 -c "import yaml,glob,os;d=yaml.safe_load(open('native/ios/project.yml'));listed={s['path'] for s in d['targets']['Continuum']['sources']};print('unlisted:',[os.path.basename(p) for p in glob.glob('native/ios/*.swift') if os.path.basename(p) not in listed])"
cd .work/artwork-probe && python3 make-harness.py && swiftc -O -o harness Extracted.swift main.swift && ./harness
